description_long:
In this inspiring talk, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Mahāgosiṅga Sutta, where six senior disciples gather in the moonlit Gosiṅgasāla wood and discuss what kind of meditator could illuminate such a beautiful place. Each disciple offers a different perspective: Ānanda emphasizes learning and teaching the Dhamma; Revata advocates for solitary meditation in empty dwellings; Anuruddha speaks of developing psychic powers like the divine eye; Mahākassapa promotes the austere forest-dwelling life; Moggallāna suggests deep discussions of Abhidhamma; and Sāriputta describes mastery over the mind (citta). When they approach the Buddha for his judgment, he validates all their answers but then offers his own profound teaching: true illumination comes from the unwavering determination to sit until complete liberation is achieved—the very resolve he made under the Bodhi tree. This sutta beautifully illustrates different valid approaches to practice while highlighting the supreme importance of decisive commitment to Awakening. The teaching offers both inspiration for dedicated practitioners and insight into the diversity of skillful means within the tradition.
